course_title: Special Topics: Cross-listed: Jews of the U.S. South
subject: HIST
course_description: Selected topics in history for students in non-history originating (cross-listed) courses. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.
course_notes: (Same as JS 271W 1) This course explores the history and culture of Jews in the U.S. South from the 18th century to the present. We will examine the impact of region on ethnic and religious identity, asking how the particular social, political, economic, and racial/ethnic setting of the South created a context for Jewish life different than that in other parts of the country, particularly in the urban North and Midwest where most American Jews concentrated. An optional visit to some relevant local historical sites will be offered, schedules permitting. Assignments include some short homework questions about the readings, one short (5 page) essay where students reflect more significantly on one week's readings, and a longer final research paper (approx. 10 pages) in which students can explore a topic of interest. This course fulfills the Continuing Writing/Continuing Communication Requirement.
